channel.title: Diffbrief · Inference
channel.description: Daily inference stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: T²Quant allocates diffusion-model activation precision by task and timestep
item.description: T²Quant uses a label-free sensitivity signal to assign activation precision across denoising steps, improving existing quantization methods by up to 6.7 percentage points at the same bit-width budget. This offers a practical path to better accuracy under fixed inference-precision constraints.

item.title: A learned unmasking policy improves diffusion language model accuracy and throughput
item.description: On LLaDA-8B-Instruct, an 856K-parameter policy using confidence and hidden states achieves the best accuracy–NFE frontier and highest GSM8K throughput; about a 10% NFE reduction offsets policy overhead in tested settings. The study gives concrete guidance for trading decoding work against speed and accuracy.

item.title: TensorRT Global Performance Tuner improves workloads by up to 1.63x
item.description: The tuner searches build routes, filters candidates that fail accuracy or crash, and selects the fastest eligible engine; ten workloads improved 1.14x–1.63x over the default route. The measured gains and accuracy-constrained tuning process are directly useful for inference optimization.

item.title: ThinkingCap cuts Gemma-4 thinking tokens by 39% on average
item.description: Across twelve benchmarks, the modified Gemma model used 38.9% fewer thinking tokens on average with a 0.15 percentage-point accuracy cost, using the same vLLM serving stack. This gives inference teams a measured efficiency trade-off to investigate.

item.title: GPU demand rarely fits the fixed rectangles of capacity contracts
item.description: Modal’s CEO discusses how GPU demand differs from contracts that reserve a fixed number of GPUs for a fixed period, and the infrastructure economics behind the company’s growth. The mismatch matters when designing flexible capacity for AI workloads.

item.title: SF Compute aims to make GPU capacity programmable and tradable
item.description: SF Compute lets customers buy or sell GPU hours and programmatically control resources from network to memory, rather than assemble a supercompute stack themselves. The infrastructure model is relevant to teams managing access to scarce AI compute.

item.title: OpenAI models and Codex workflows are coming to Google Cloud Marketplace
item.description: OpenAI models and Codex workflows are slated for Gemini’s Model Garden through Google Cloud Marketplace. Engineers using Google Cloud will have another route to these models and coding workflows.

item.title: AI requests are estimated to emit 8.5 times more CO₂ in Texas than Sweden
item.description: An open-source method estimates emissions per AI request using average regional grid intensity, with the reported Texas-to-Sweden difference at 8.5 times. Per-request estimates could help teams include energy impacts when comparing AI providers.

item.title: Eight-node DGX Spark clusters reach 52 tokens per second on Qwen3.8-27B
item.description: The post reports decode throughput rising from about 12 to 52 tokens per second across one to eight nodes, and a RoCEnante backend delivering 4.43× decode speedup versus 3.05× without it. These measurements help teams assess multi-node inference scaling and routing trade-offs.

item.title: Test-time regression compresses sequences with 55.6% fewer visual tokens
item.description: TTR-Compressor fits a learned regression over input tokens and computes its coefficients in closed form; in multimodal models it matches the standard MLP merger with 55.6% fewer visual tokens. The technique offers a measured path to reducing visual-token processing while preserving performance.

item.title: TorchTPU opens PyTorch workloads to Google TPUs with minimal code changes
item.description: The open-source TorchTPU stack supports familiar PyTorch APIs on TPUs, with eager-mode debugging and torch.compile for production optimization; it also lists integrations including vLLM, SGLang, and Ray. Teams can evaluate TPUs without abandoning their existing model tooling.

item.title: Google Cloud adds Anthropic-managed Claude deployments with platform features
item.description: The new option runs Anthropic-managed Claude on Google Cloud infrastructure, with Google Cloud IAM, Cloud Audit Logging and access to Claude platform features. Teams can weigh processor and feature requirements when choosing how to deploy models.

item.title: Amazon Polly adds 14 generative voices across nine locales
item.description: Polly’s generative engine upgrade adds 14 voices across nine locales, including general availability in Hindi and Finnish, while keeping existing voice names and API calls unchanged. Teams using managed speech generation can adopt the change without modifying their integrations.

item.title: ALLOT allocates video-attention sparsity by each layer-step's output impact
item.description: ALLOT probes layer-step contributions to video error and optimizes sparsity under a measured-latency budget; with XAttention, it reports an 11.8 dB PSNR gain at equal or shorter wall-clock time. The method targets inference cost without replacing existing attention kernels or selection strategies.

item.title: Vocabulary specialization cuts measured SLM inference cost by 77%
item.description: VocabX specializes a model's vocabulary around the cost of each token and reports a 77% inference-cost reduction in a production essay grader without changing the base model. This challenges the assumption that tokenizers are fixed and points to a potentially high-leverage optimization for domain models.

item.title: FlyDSL speeds up PyTorch operators on AMD MI350 GPUs
item.description: FlyDSL adds AMD MI350 support for GEMM, attention, normalization, and TopK operators, with reported geometric-mean speedups ranging from 1.10× to 4.82× across the described kernel suites. The operator-level results offer practical performance evidence for teams optimizing PyTorch workloads on AMD GPUs.

item.title: TorchTPU adds a native PyTorch backend for Google TPUs
item.description: TorchTPU combines eager-execution optimizations, torch.compile integration and native TPU acceleration for model execution and migration. Engineers evaluating accelerator options can assess a new PyTorch path for training and inference.

item.title: Confidential G4 Blackwell GPU instances reach general availability in 36 zones
item.description: Google made Confidential Computing on G4 instances with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs generally available across 36 zones, including on Compute Engine VMs and GKE nodes. This expands options for processing sensitive data and models in use.

item.title: Respan builds a Rust AI gateway with plugin-based features
item.description: Respan separates providers, protocols, modalities, and gateway features into plugins around a small core. The modular approach is relevant to teams assembling AI gateways, though the listing offers no comparative performance data.

item.title: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, its production inference framework
item.description: The roundup reports that DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer, its production serving stack, with prompt caching of up to 72 hours; the title also claims 155T tokens per day per cluster. Open production inference code and long-lived caching could inform serving-cost and throughput decisions.

item.title: DeepInfer releases a production inference framework for DeepSeek models
item.description: DeepInfer lists optimized kernels, parallelism strategies, asynchronous scheduling, deterministic sampling and confidence-scheduled draft verification. Its production-serving focus and concrete inference features make it relevant to engineers building high-throughput model services.

item.title: Google open-sources TorchTPU, a PyTorch backend for TPUs
item.description: TorchTPU provides ATen kernels, a compilation cache, distributed training support and examples for model inference, with integration for torch.compile(). It gives engineers a new route to running PyTorch workloads on Google TPUs.

item.title: SolarRenderer generates structured video in four steps, 12.3 times faster than 50-step sampling
item.description: Two lightweight LoRAs adapt a frozen video backbone to structural inputs, enabling four-step rendering; a block-causal variant renders 768p video in real time. The design shows how to add controllable generation while reducing sampling steps.

item.title: VLA-Rolling reuses discarded action tails to reduce denoising cost
item.description: The framework carries unexecuted action tails into the next planning round and allocates refinement steps using per-action confidence; it lowers inference cost across all 16 tested model–benchmark pairs. Adaptive reuse could reduce the latency and compute cost of iterative action generation.

item.title: TorchTPU runs Hugging Face models natively on Google TPUs
item.description: TorchTPU makes TPU a native PyTorch device for Transformers, Diffusers and Kernels, avoiding a port to torch_xla or JAX. This could simplify moving existing model workloads onto TPU hardware.

item.title: PyTorch 2.15 adds FP8 and faster decoding paths to MPS
item.description: The MPS update adds FP8, faster language-model decoding paths through linear layers and softmax, and dedicated Metal kernels for audio, video and training. These backend changes matter to engineers running models on Apple hardware.

item.title: TorchNeuron makes AWS Trainium a native PyTorch device
item.description: TorchNeuron is an open-source backend that lets developers program Trainium as a standard PyTorch device, using PyTorch APIs for training and serving libraries. This could simplify adapting AI workloads to Trainium without replacing their PyTorch-based stack.

item.title: TorchNeuron brings native PyTorch support to AWS Trainium
item.description: TorchNeuron adds eager mode, torch.compile, and distributed APIs including FSDP and tensor parallelism, with support in Transformers, Diffusers, and Kernels. This could make Trainium easier to adopt across model workflows built on PyTorch.

item.title: Jane Street and NVIDIA optimize three Mamba-2 forward-pass kernels with cuTile
item.description: The implementation uses cuTile for three Mamba-2 kernels, including Tensor Core matrix multiplication to advance hidden state across sequence chunks. The kernel design offers practical material for engineers optimizing GPU execution of state-space models.

item.title: LLM proxies can expose token-usage telemetry missing from provider frontends
item.description: It argues that provider interfaces show distracting activity rather than the time-series token statistics engineers need. That visibility matters when diagnosing usage and making decisions about LLM-backed systems.

item.title: Mercury 3 claims 1,068 tokens per second with a million-token context
item.description: Inception says its diffusion-based LLM reaches 1,068 tokens per second on NVIDIA GPUs, supports a one-million-token context, and costs $0.20 per million input tokens. The release is a concrete claim to evaluate against serving latency, quality, and cost requirements.

item.title: vLLM 0.32 adds broader low-precision KV cache support and parser updates
item.description: The release adds NVFP4 and 4-bit KV cache options across GPU architectures; one GLM-5.x configuration halves KV memory per rank with 2.3–5.5% more throughput but 7–11% higher TTFT. These trade-offs help serving teams tune memory, throughput and latency.

item.title: DLite removes historical KV-cache dependence from speculative decoding
item.description: DLite uses target-model hidden states for local speculative prediction instead of maintaining historical context; existing draft models lose up to 80% of acceptance length on agentic workloads. The approach targets both acceptance degradation and KV-cache overhead in multi-turn serving.

item.title: Speculative sampling uses large video windows without waiting for chunk boundaries
item.description: The method pads larger bidirectional windows with noise latents, caches predictions while conditions stay unchanged and delivers results incrementally with replaceable future frames. It reframes the latency–quality trade-off for interactive video generation, but the excerpt reports no measured gains.

item.title: Muse Spark Open arrives in SageMaker JumpStart with BF16 and NVFP4 variants
item.description: The coding-optimized model is available as BF16 and NVFP4 variants, with a one-million-token context, and can be deployed to a SageMaker endpoint. The variants and managed deployment path are useful details when evaluating model-serving options.

item.title: An eBPF GPU-server request loop matched an efficient epoll baseline
item.description: The bpf-gpu-server moves TCP handling into eBPF and io_uring so no user thread reads, schedules or sends requests, yet CPU use and latency matched an efficient epoll server. The comparison helps identify when kernel-bypass complexity is unlikely to improve a GPU serving path.

item.title: Llmspeed estimates local LLM performance across hardware and models
item.description: Llmspeed lets users browse local LLM speed estimates by hardware and model, drawing on community benchmark measurements. It can help engineers compare candidate setups before buying hardware, though the excerpt gives no specific performance results.

item.title: Muse Spark Open targets agentic coding with 1M context and NVFP4 weights
item.description: Muse Spark Open activates 42B of 816B parameters per token, uses a 1M-token context and NVFP4 checkpoints, and is reported to reach 50K tokens/s per GPU on GB300 NVL72. These figures matter when evaluating large MoE models and hardware for agent serving.

item.title: Muse Spark Open reaches 36 tokens per second across four Mac Studios with MLX
item.description: Apple reports over 36 tokens per second for the nearly trillion-parameter Muse Spark Open on four Mac Studios, using MLX and RDMA over Thunderbolt at an 8,192-token context. The setup offers a concrete reference for distributed inference on unified-memory hardware.

item.title: PS5LM serves GGUF models from a jailbroken PS5 using llama.cpp
item.description: PS5LM runs llama.cpp's Vulkan backend on the PS5 GPU, uses 11.4 GB of shared memory, and exposes OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs to devices on the network. It is a concrete edge-inference deployment, though tied to jailbroken console hardware.

item.title: MJev-Spatial replaces spatial answer generation with one-pass classification
item.description: MJev-Spatial scores candidate answers using pretrained query and key projections, handling choices, numeric values, and points without generating answer tokens. A single forward pass for each decision could reduce latency in spatial tasks that require frequent interaction.

item.title: Beam serving on Google Cloud reports up to 5× higher performance and 8× lower latency
item.description: Google Cloud and Reflection report up to 5× higher performance and 8× lower latency for Beam using llm-d with vLLM or NVIDIA Dynamo with SGLang. The serving recipes and reported gains are relevant to teams running large models for agent workloads.

item.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark brings local coding agents and model customization to one PC
item.description: RTX Spark pairs a GB10 system-on-chip with up to 128GB of unified memory for running coding agents, fine-tuning models, and deploying locally. A single-machine setup could simplify local agent development and testing.

item.title: Speculative Forcing stops denoising tokens once their outputs are stable
item.description: Speculative Forcing accepts tokens early when a verifier judges their intermediate estimates sufficiently close to final outputs, while retaining their cached keys and values. It reports matching the four-step LongLive generator with about 1.7 denoising steps, a promising route to cheaper video generation.

item.title: Velox routes video-world attention by spatial memory and speeds chunk 48 denoising 2.43×
item.description: Velox uses camera-frustum overlap to select historical context, reporting 4.36× faster attention and 2.43× faster denoising at chunk 48. The approach targets growing KV-cache costs in long interactive video rollouts.

item.title: ExecuTorch runs TinyML models on Cortex-M with under 90 KiB of RAM
item.description: The Cortex-M backend runs four MLPerf Tiny models on an Alif Ensemble E8 in 21.5 ms or less, using under 90 KiB of RAM; the core runtime is under 20 KiB of flash. This shows a single PyTorch workflow can reach tightly constrained devices without a framework conversion step.

item.title: KV4-RL protects selected KV positions to speed INT4 rollouts
item.description: KV4-RL keeps attention sinks and recent context in INT8 while quantizing the rest to INT4, achieving 1.80× cumulative rollout speedup and 1.27× full-iteration speedup with final accuracy within 0.5 percentage points of BF16. The results show how selective KV-cache protection can improve RL training throughput while limiting quality loss.

item.title: SageMaker JumpStart adds repeatable model deployment and performance testing
item.description: The guide deploys a pretrained model, runs a lightweight performance test with the SageMaker SDK and removes the endpoint afterward. Named endpoint configurations target low cost, low latency or general-purpose workloads.

item.title: DoSA skips unnecessary sparse-attention scores with exact selection guarantees
item.description: DoSA uses score bounds to avoid fully scoring candidates that cannot enter Top-K, reporting up to 2.74× Indexer speedup and up to 1.94× time-to-first-token speedup. Its exact-selection approach offers a concrete path to faster sparse-attention serving.

item.title: PyTorch Inductor replaces Spyre’s custom compiler stack with one 7× smaller
item.description: IBM moved Spyre’s torch.compile backend from a separately built stack to an Inductor backend, leaving most of Inductor unchanged and shrinking the compiler about 7×. It’s a concrete example of adapting a shared compiler to a non-GPU inference accelerator.

item.title: Pulse Local uses small on-device models to answer questions about spending
item.description: A tuned Qwen3 0.6B model turns spending questions into structured queries, code handles the arithmetic, and a 4B model checks answers, with disagreement prompting uncertainty. This is a concrete pattern for keeping sensitive data local while limiting model errors.

item.title: Indra OCR reports 49 pages per second on 32 CPU cores
item.description: Indra OCR pairs a 1M-parameter recognizer with layout boxes, labels and reading order, reporting 49 pages per second on 32 CPU cores and higher OmniParseBench scores than Tesseract and PP-OCR. Its CPU throughput and structured output may make document ingestion cheaper and easier to integrate.

item.title: Fused MoE kernels combine routing and expert computation into GPU operations
item.description: The post describes fused MoE operations that combine token routing, data shuffling, and expert computation, and discusses hardware-specific kernel optimizations. Efficient MoE kernels can directly affect inference latency and cost, though the excerpt gives no performance results.

item.title: A browser RAG demo retrieves four passages and summarizes them locally
item.description: The demo combines in-browser semantic search with a small language model that summarizes the four most relevant passages, and measures answer faithfulness. Local execution keeps typed questions on the user's machine; the excerpt does not give the measurement results.

item.title: Intel D270 offers up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X for inference
item.description: Intel describes a 350 W, air-cooled PCIe accelerator with up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X, aimed at long contexts and concurrent agent sessions. The specifications are relevant to inference capacity planning, though no independent performance results are provided.

item.title: ReplaySSM speeds hybrid-model decoding with checkpointed state and input buffers
item.description: ReplaySSM stores a checkpoint plus recent inputs, cutting state-memory traffic roughly in half and speeding decoding kernels 1.46–1.80x; speculative throughput rises 1.85–2.10x. The design targets memory traffic, rollback, and precision trade-offs in hybrid-model serving.

item.title: Janas streams model experts from SSD and reports 24 tok/s on a 48 GB model
item.description: On a 32 GB laptop, Janas reports 24 tok/s generating with a 48 GB Qwen3-Next-80B model, versus 2.8 tok/s for llama.cpp, and also reports faster prompt processing. The results could inform trade-offs for running models larger than available RAM.

item.title: An iPad app runs an unmodified Linux AMD GPU driver for on-device inference
item.description: The app bundles the upstream Linux amdgpu and amdkfd drivers in a PCIDriverKit extension, then runs its inference engine on an AMD GPU in a Thunderbolt enclosure. The design is a notable example of bringing GPU inference to an iPad.

item.title: DCOCO restores context across parallel speculative drafts
item.description: DCOCO keeps multiple draft-token candidates and checks their compatibility across positions in parallel, restoring context among draft tokens at low additional cost. Its throughput results across four verifier backbones and ten benchmarks make it relevant to speculative-decoding design.

item.title: Bedrock routes OpenAI GPT inference across Regions in five Asian markets
item.description: The guide configures global cross-Region inference for Bedrock-hosted GPT models and covers API calls, permissions, and monitoring. This offers serving teams a path around capacity limits in a single Region.

item.title: SageMaker serves llama.cpp decision models with probabilities over fixed choices
item.description: The guide uses llama.cpp on SageMaker for text generation and extends the runtime with SemIf to return probabilities over declared options without decoding an answer token. That pattern suits agent routing and other systems that need scores over actions rather than generated text.

item.title: LatentGRM cuts reward-judge inference time by up to 7x
item.description: LatentGRM compresses evaluation trajectories by 8.9–9.2x and reduces judge inference time by 6.1–7.0x at vote@5, with competitive preference accuracy against explicit SFT judges. It shows how rubric-guided latent reasoning can lower the cost of model evaluation.

item.title: PreSTO batches speculative proposals without changing PowerMH sampling
item.description: PreSTO batches prefetched Metropolis–Hastings proposals while preserving PowerMH's transition kernel, reporting median speedups of 1.71×, 1.91× and 2.33× across seven datasets and five base LLMs. The approach targets sequential sampling overhead without changing the sampler's behavior.

item.title: SoloQ enables calibration-free quantization for diffusion language models
item.description: SoloQ rotates weights and activations into a predictable distribution for data-independent low-bit quantization, and applies commit-time KV-cache quantization to block-diffusion models. Calibration-free deployment could simplify quantization where activations shift across denoising steps.

item.title: BetterWispr runs speech transcription locally on a Mac
item.description: The open-source dictation tool uses built-in models on the Mac, works offline after model downloads, and has no cloud fallback. It is a concrete example of local inference for a user-facing application, though the listing gives no performance details.

item.title: Fixed-choice decision models select an answer in one forward pass
item.description: The approach masks all but a fixed set of answer tokens and picks the highest-probability option in one pass, instead of generating a constrained response token by token. This can make structured, fixed-option answers faster to produce.

item.title: A corruption-lattice cost predicts the minimum steps for generative decoding
item.description: The paper models decoding schedules as paths on a corruption lattice and defines their cost by discarded dependence; for Markov data on a graph, zero-cost schedules require steps equal to the graph's treedepth. This offers a way to assess decoding schedules before running them.

item.title: SpecFold reuses shared computation across diffusion-model draft branches
item.description: SpecFold uses token-level residual gating to reuse parent attention and FFN computation across speculative branches, with a Triton kernel for sparse execution and reported throughput gains. The algorithm-system co-design targets a distinct source of inference cost in diffusion language models.
